### Changed

- **The tests of the repository no longer run on macOS for now**: the macOS job was taken out of the CI workflow (every pull request, every push to main, every tag and the nightly run test on Ubuntu and Windows), and the workflow says that macOS support will be taken up again later. Nothing of the monitor changes.
- **The frozen shape of the API goes one level deeper**: the keys of the nested objects of the read answers (the cycle and the credential of the health, the loop of the data, the folders, the links, the update notice, the counters of the status bar and of the alerts), the exact `code` of the error of an unknown repository, the health of one repository and the envelope of the sentinel answers are part of the contract now. The check tool follows nested objects, and the test feeds a server with the invented data of the demo to check the answers that need data.
- **Forks and archived repositories are chosen by a setting, and a maintained fork is never lost**: `discovery.skip_archived` (on by default) decides whether archived repositories are watched; `discovery.fork_policy` can leave forks out (`skip`) or keep only the ones that have a CI of their own (`skip_unless_ci`: an enabled workflow and a run inside `discovery.fork_ci_days`), and `auto` does the same with a window twice as long on an organisation, whose kind is read once a day; `discovery.fork_checks_per_pass` limits the requests spent on it. The default (`show`) changes nothing.
- **The check of release files adapts to the project**: `sentinel.surface.checks.release_assets.require_sha256` and `.require_signature` stop asking for a checksum or a signature file, `.allow_empty` accepts a release without files (projects that publish to a package registry), `sentinel.surface.checks.tag_vs_version.prefixes` compares tags such as `cli-v1.2.0` with the manifest, and `.prerelease_ok` treats the betas of one day of a calendar version as the same version; `sentinel.require_verified_signature` was already switchable. The defaults ask for what they asked before.
- **A red on the default branch only counts when the repository itself caused it**: only runs of the events `push`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` and `merge_group` decide (setting `ci.red_events`), and a run of a pull request that comes from a fork never does, even when the branch of the fork is also called `main`, `master` or `dev` (setting `ci.count_fork_runs`). The same rule feeds the red tile, the alerts, the team view, the brief and the green-without-release check.
- **A run that waits for an approval is its own state, not a red and not a queue**: `action_required` (a pull request of a fork or a first contribution that nobody approved) and a job held by the protection of an environment no longer turn a workflow red or inflate the queued count; the Now tab shows a separate line "waiting for approval" and the figures carry `awaiting`.
- **An abandoned workflow is "inactive", not red for ever**: a workflow whose last run failed but which has not run for `ci.inactive_days` days (90 by default, 0 turns it off) leaves the red list and is counted in the `inactive` figure.
- **Workflows that only react to issues, comments or labels do not count as red CI**: they are told apart by the events they run on (setting `ci.automation_counts`, off by default); every red row now says which kind of workflow it is.
- **The release gate checks the zip against the versioned files**: the zip must hold exactly the files the repository versions in the product folder (the example configuration, which the build makes, is the only exception); a versioned file that would not travel, whatever its suffix or folder, and a stray file that would travel without being versioned both stop the release. A short list of intended exclusions (`NOT_SHIPPED`) is empty. A test also covers the rule that every data file under `src/` travels.
- **Hygiene (A6) no longer assumes the conventions of one owner**: the name of the ruleset is a setting (`sentinel.hygiene.ruleset_names`, patterns allowed); `sentinel.hygiene.ruleset_mode` can judge the default branch by the rules GitHub reports as in force (public endpoints, no admin rights needed) whatever the ruleset is called; `sentinel.hygiene.skip` leaves a check out; `sentinel.hygiene.community_fallback` also counts the community profile and the `.github` repository of the account; a licence called LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE.txt, COPYING or recognised by GitHub is accepted; and what the token cannot know (no admin rights) is shown as not evaluable, never green and never a warning. The defaults keep the old rule.
- **A2 settles many workflows with one request**: a repository with at least `sentinel.a2_resolve_batch_min` workflows to look up (2 by default; 0 = one by one) is asked once for its newest completed runs of the default branch, pull requests left out, and every workflow found in them is settled together (`sentinel.a2_resolve_batch_pages` pages of 100 at most); what the list does not show is asked one by one as before, so a repository with 100 or more workflows converges in a few cycles instead of four workflows per cycle.
- **The health of the team is fast with thousands of repositories**: the runs, red workflows, running runs and alerts are grouped by repository once, so a request to the team health no longer walks all of them for each repository (2,000 repositories took about eight seconds), and the health of one repository builds only its own view.

### Fixed

- **A group of the readiness chips says why it has no number, and a repository without any workflow no longer lowers its coverage**: a repository whose clone has no workflow file and which has no run is "not applicable": it is left out of the coverage of its group (so a group of five where two are new and empty is measured on the other three) and is listed apart in the tooltip and in the table. A group that is still below `sentinel.readiness.min_coverage` shows the words "not enough data" (not a bare "?") and its tooltip says how many repositories have data against the minimum and which ones lack it. The default minimum is not changed.
- **The account score says how long the calibration lasts and why something is missing**: while it calibrates the chip says how much is left of `score.calibrating_hours` with a bar and the day and hour the number will appear (`data_quality.calibrating_hours` is new), "not enough data" says which condition fails (runs or coverage), and `GET /api/score` carries `missing_detail` with the reason a part is not counted (its sentinel is off, it has not finished its first sweep and how many repositories it has read, it has read too few, its sources cannot be read, or the data is ready for the next pass).
- **The ring of the last 24 hours counts from one source and never shows a negative number**: the total in the centre and the three figures of the legend (successful, failed, cancelled or other) come from the server (`figures.done24` is new) and always add up; before, the total was counted on the list of runs the page receives, which holds only the newest ones, and "cancelled or other" went negative. A figure that is negative or not a number is drawn as 0, and when the server does not send the total the three figures are counted on the list and the card says it is a sample. The success rate per repository says the same when its list is a sample.
- **A score ledger that cannot be read is never written over**: when the ledger of the score exists but cannot be read after the retries (Windows, a file held by a backup or an antivirus), the hourly pass does nothing and the problem is noted in the health of the monitor; the last good ledger stays and the next pass reads it again. It used to start from an empty ledger and replace the good one.
- **The report schedule at its edges**: the hour that happens twice when the clock goes back in autumn no longer produces two reports, a monthly report (or a yearly one) that was owed while the monitor was stopped for more than eight days is still written, and a report whose second format cannot be written leaves no file of the first one behind.
- **The log of actions also records what is confirmed on GitHub and on this computer**: a rerun, cancel, dispatch or merge on GitHub (with its action, repository and number), a run with `act`, saving or deleting the stored token, a change of the working mode, a group added by discovery, a lesson or a book of failures added, a report written now, the change of the login of an account and the actions of the AI. Each line has the person, the result and the status, never the body. Every POST route is now either recorded or listed as exempt with its reason (`security/audited_posts.py`) and a test fails when a new route is neither. A silence that could not be created or removed is no longer logged as done, and its line is written once the silence exists.
- **Several processes writing the same file work again on Windows**: the owner of a lock file tries again for about a second to delete it when Windows refuses (a reader had it open), and a lock file younger than a second is no longer opened to read the number of its process (a live owner lets go of it in milliseconds). Before, the lock stayed for 30 seconds while the others gave up after 10, and the writers of the feed, of the log of actions and of the reports failed under load.
- **A lock file left by a writer that died is taken over at once**: the lock file of the file storage holds the number of its process; when that process no longer exists the next writer takes the lock immediately (it used to wait 30 seconds, longer than its own 10-second limit, and failed), and the takeover is logged. When the process cannot be known the age of the file still decides, and that time can be changed with `MONITOR_LOCK_STALE`. A test kills a writer inside the lock and checks that the feed is writable again.
- **Durations and queue times of re-run workflows are no longer absurd**: the wait in the queue and the duration are measured on the latest attempt of a run (`run_attempt`); the creation time of the first try is never used for a re-run, so queues of days and durations of hundreds of days no longer reach the analytics panel, the stuck-run check or the exports. A duration longer than the 35 days a run can last is left empty. The new setting `ci.rerun_timing` (off by default) also asks GitHub for the real duration of finished re-runs.
- **A try after an approval is not "flaky"**: a run that needed a person to approve it (`action_required`) and then passed, and the runs of pull requests that come from forks, no longer count as flaky workflows.
- The failing job of a run with more than 30 jobs is found: the lists of jobs that the alert for an AI, the assistant and the batch tool read were cut at 30 and are now cut at 100 (the same single request).
- **A clock set back no longer stops the score, the purge and the scheduled reports**: a saved moment that lies in the future (a computer without a battery clock that starts with an old date, or a clock corrected by hand) is no longer believed; the pass is due at once and writes a good moment, instead of waiting for days until the old clock is reached again.

### Security

- **One cleaner for everything an AI can read**: the text the integrated assistant sends to a provider, the repository, workflow, link and conclusion of every alert, `GET /api/ai/state`, `GET /api/ai/alerts`, `GET /api/ai/brief?fmt=json`, the feed file, its state file and the body of the hook all go through the same cleaner (before, a password in `DB_PASSWORD=...`, a user and key inside an address, an `sk-` key, a token, an e-mail address, an IP address or the home folder could go out). A test plants a secret of each kind and fails if one shows up in any of those outputs.
- **The integrated assistant keeps its key and stays on this computer**: a call to a provider no longer follows a redirect (the key would have gone on to the other address; the redirect is reported as the answer of the provider) and no longer uses the proxy variables of the environment, so a local server such as Ollama is really called directly. A remote provider goes through the proxy only with `network.use_proxy`.
- **The cleaner knows more forms of a secret**: PGP key blocks, `--password value` and `mysql -phunter2` on a command line, cookies, `Authorization: Basic ...`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY=`, `SENTRY_DSN=` and `AWS_CREDS=`, a value with escaped quotes, a phrase after `password:`, a token cut by a line break, `sk_live_` keys, compressed IPv6 addresses, network shares and the folder of root; text hidden behind an encoding (percent codes, zero-width characters, full-width letters) is cleaned too, and a pair whose key says it is a secret (`{"password": ...}`) is replaced whole. It is a cleaner by pattern: the guide and the skills no longer promise that nothing can get through.
- **Text of third parties is data, not an instruction**: the line that the gate script of an AI tool copies for each alert keeps the repository name only if it is one and cuts the workflow name to a short plain text; a lesson that an AI wrote goes between the delimiters of untrusted data in the prompt of the integrated assistant; a stranger's text (the title of an issue) mentions nobody in Discord and is escaped for Slack.
- **Apprise**: leftover folders with the addresses of the services are swept at the first send, a comma inside an address no longer cuts it, and each address is written quoted.
- **The presets file is validated like the settings page**: only listed fields are served, addresses must be accepted by the page, a cloud preset cannot point to this computer or a private address, and the variable of the key cannot be one of the system or of the monitor (`GH_TOKEN`, `PATH`, `MONITOR_*`...); the same rule applies to the setting `ai.api_key_env`.
- **The process of each account no longer keeps the key of the supervisor and the access token in its environment**: both leave the environment at the very start of every process (monitor, supervisor and account), before the first `gh` or any other program is started, also when the access token has another name. The comment that promised the secrets would be hidden from the process list of Linux now states its real limit.
- **The image can no longer carry the data of whoever builds it**: the build context excluded the loose files of the old layout but not the `config/`, `data/`, `logs/` and `ai/` folders where the tokens, users, sessions and settings live now; they are excluded, the app stage of the Dockerfile deletes them too, and a test checks both against the list of folders of the product.
- **Three visitors with wrong tokens can no longer lock everybody out behind the reverse proxy**: the lock shared by the whole proxy counts only the requests that arrive without a usable `X-Forwarded-For`; a request that carries the address of its visitor is counted against that address alone, the shared lock ends after the lock time and never stops a request that carries the right access token.
- **The time of a login no longer tells which names are users**: a user who is locked costs the same work as a name that does not exist, so "locked" answers in the same time for both.
- **A path under `/api/accounts/` that the supervisor does not filter is judged like any other route**: only the list, the status and the credential of an account skip the account check of the gate, and the credential of an account is refused to a user who cannot see that account.
- **The log of actions keeps one chain when several processes write the same file**: each line is chained to the last line that is really in the file, read under a lock between processes (only the end of the file is read), and that lock also waits when Windows answers "access denied" while another process deletes the lock file.
- **The log of actions is one file for each account**: in the Complete edition with several accounts the processes of different accounts wrote the same `audit_actions.jsonl` (and an administrator of one account could read lines of another); each account now keeps its own file in its folder and `GET /api/audit-log` keeps only the lines of the account that answers. The lines written before stay in the old shared file, which the supervisor still reads.
- **The check of the log of actions covers the rotated file too**: `chain` verifies `audit_actions.jsonl.1` and the link between it and the active file, names the segment (`segment`) when a line is broken, says how many segments it checked (`segments`) and whether the chain begins at its first link (`complete`).
- **The log of actions can no longer be read by a viewer, and it records more of what matters**: the route needs at least the maintainer role at the door (an administrator, or a maintainer when `audit_log.maintainers_can_read` is on, still decides inside), switching the log off writes its own last line, a line that cannot be written is counted and shown (`write_failures`, `last_write_error_at` in `GET /api/audit-log`, and a degradation notice), and failed changes of one's own password stay in the audit of the accesses instead of filling the log of actions.

### Added

- **The notification event `ai_alert`**: a new real alert from a panel or a signal of the monitor can reach the notification channels (add `ai_alert` to `notify.events`; off by default). A red workflow keeps its own event, `red_new`.

### Changed

- **The score now penalizes a failure that is not fixed**: the recovery part counts a workflow that is still red at the end of the window with the time it has been red so far (a lower bound that grows while the red lasts), instead of leaving it out. Before, an account that never fixed its red could score better than one that fixed it in a day. Expect lower numbers for accounts that have a workflow in red when you update. `docs/SCORE.md` explains it in the eight languages.

### Fixed

- **The score and the score ledger**: a re-run of a run is counted as one more execution (GitHub keeps the id, so the first conclusion used to stay for ever); the calculation no longer divides by zero when no part has data (the answer is `insufficient_data` with the reason `no_data`); when the ledger drops runs past 20000 and that reaches the current window the snapshot says so (`data_quality.truncated`); the mean of `GET /api/score/global` leaves out stale snapshots (counted in `accounts_stale`) and `/metrics` does not export `ghamon_score` for them; and the score guide now describes five parts, with `score.weights.security`, in the eight languages.
- **The Security sentinel no longer passes "could not read" for "clean"**: when most of the sources that weigh in the penalty (Dependabot, code scanning, secrets) answer 403 or 404 for every repository, the level is `unknown` instead of `ok` and the security part of the score is left out instead of counting as 100 (the status carries `sources_readable` and `sources_total`). A source that stops answering while an alert is open keeps the alert for a week, marked as unread, and never announces it as fixed; a `gh` that prints nothing is a failed reading, and a default branch with a slash in its name is asked for encoded.
- **A few repositories that always fail no longer starve the Security sentinel**: a repository whose reads fail waits 5 minutes, 30 minutes and then 6 hours before the next try, and the ones not tried yet go first, so the rest of the account is looked at.
- **A repository that the sentinels could not look at is no longer shown as OK in the health of the team**: when every sentinel is in error, paused or degraded (or all are off and nothing has run for a week), a quiet repository is `unknown` ("Not seen"), the ranking rows carry `not_fully_seen` with the names of the sentinels that could not read it, the totals count them, and the Team tab marks the state with an asterisk and a hint. A red workflow or an alert still make it `warn` or `bad`.
- **One damaged byte in the event feed no longer stops the notifications**: past 512 KB the feed was read again as strict UTF-8 to trim it, a single invalid byte raised an error that escaped, the feed grew without a limit and every new event failed before reaching the channels. The trim now reads tolerantly and can never stop the channels.
- **A file in use no longer reads as empty in the files storage**: on Windows a backup, an antivirus or an editor can hold a file for a moment; the reader took the file for empty and the next save wrote on top of it (users, score ledger records, score snapshots, analytics). A file that exists is now read again a few times, and whoever reads to change and save stops with an error instead of overwriting. Several processes appending to the same event feed take a lock between processes, so no line is lost or cut on Windows.
- **Repeating `migrate_storage` no longer replaces newer data in the target**: an account whose target has newer events or snapshots is reported as `target newer`, refused without writing anything, and the exit code is 1; `--force` makes the source win. The run also prints a warning with the count of damaged lines of the event feed that it cannot copy (the source keeps them).
- **A backup is checked completely before a restore writes anything**: an account id or a name that is not valid anywhere in the copy makes `verify` fail, so a restore can no longer stop half way with the first accounts already written.
- **An answer of the MCP server that is longer than its limit is still a valid document**: rows are left out of the longest list instead of cutting the text, the answer says `truncated` and how many rows are missing, and the health signals (old data, degraded monitor, allowance) are the last to go.
- **A number that is not a number no longer cuts the connection**: `?since=`, `?limit=` and `Last-Event-ID` accept only the digits 0-9 (and at most 15); anything else is the default.
- **The state of the scheduled reports is shared safely by several accounts**: each account changes its entry under a lock, and a replace that a reader blocks for a moment on Windows is tried again.
- **The tables of the skills say which calls are only for this computer**: the table is generated from the same lists the server uses, and `/api/ai/failures` lists its POST. A report no longer carries raw titles: the titles of alerts go through the cleaner and Markdown does not turn an address into a link by itself.
- **The API contract now covers `/api/data` and cannot be trimmed**: the route that gives the runs, the repositories and the allowance was not in the frozen contract. It is now, the routes that are readable but not frozen are listed under `unfrozen` with their reason, a test fails when a new GET route is in neither list, and another compares the contract with the one of the first 2.x version so that a path, a key or a type cannot disappear in the same commit that breaks the API.
- **The window of a repository opened from the Team tab showed nothing**: a row of the ranking carries only the name, and the page asked the health of the repository with an empty owner; it now uses the owner of the page. The deep link `?view=repo&repo=owner/name` also no longer fills the text filter of the Now tab with the repository, which left that tab empty.
- **A workflow, job or repository name with brackets no longer breaks the terminal views**: `test [ubuntu, 3.13]` was shown as `test`, `docs [/api]` ended the view with an error, and a name could carry styles or links of the terminal. The names are drawn as plain text in both views, and a picture that cannot be drawn is skipped instead of ending the view.
- **An empty Enter at the menu of the Windows batch launcher repeated the last option**: choosing 2 and pressing Enter again fired the whole batch a second time, because `set /p` keeps the old value when nothing is typed. The variable is cleared before each question, and a test runs the real launcher.
- **Scripts with a shebang had Windows line endings in the published zip**: the 33 `.py` files that start with `#!` (the entry points of `bin/` among them) could not be run directly on Linux or macOS when the zip was built on Windows. The zip now carries them with LF and the release gate fails if one still has a CR in its first line.

### Fixed

- **The published zip lacked the AI presets file**: the packaging now includes every data file of the package and the release gate fails if one is missing from the zip.

- **An untranslated state key on the all-accounts page**: the two missing keys are now in the eight catalogues, and a test checks that every `ui` key used by the page exists in the eight catalogues.

### Added

- **The contract of the read API, frozen from here on**: `docs/schemas/api_contract.json` lists the 37 read endpoints with the keys and the types of their answers in each edition (and which of them the Lite edition answers with `404`) and the error codes of the door (`401 access`, `403 forbidden`, `404`). A key listed there keeps its name and its type for the whole of 2.x; new keys may appear and nothing is removed without a new major version. The suite `test_200_contract.py` checks it against a real server of each edition and also the rules of the door: a foreign `Host` is `403`, the network mode asks for the token in the header `X-Monitor-Access` and answers `401 access` without it, the words of a query that nobody reads are ignored and every answer is JSON in UTF-8.

- **A tool to check any running monitor against the contract**: `python tools/check_api_contract.py` (`--lite`, `--url`, `--token-file`) reads the contract, asks the monitor with `GET` only, prints one line for each key that is missing or has another type and ends with `CONTRACT=PASS` or `CONTRACT=FAIL` (exit code 0, 1, or 2 when nobody answers). It is for the people whose scripts, wall screens or mobile clients depend on the answers, after each upgrade of the monitor or of the client. It makes no call to GitHub.

- **The interfaces for sentinels and storages are frozen by a test too**: `test_200_interfaces.py` fixes the nine fields of an `Alert`, the methods of `BaseSentinel` and of `Storage` with the names of their parameters, the kinds of record, and that both storages and the three sentinels implement every method. A change there is a change of contract.

- **One guide for each use, in the eight languages**: Complete for one person (`COMPLETE_INDIVIDUAL.md`), Complete as a service (`COMPLETE_SERVICE.md`), Complete for a team (`COMPLETE_TEAM.md`) and the API for clients (`API.md`), next to the short guide of the Lite edition. They are in the Help panel, in the list of guides of the README, and a test checks that they exist in the eight languages, that their links resolve and that every setting and endpoint they name exists. A second test reads every guide of the documentation in the eight languages and fails when one names a route that the code does not have.

### Changed

- **Version 2.0.0, the monitor is declared mature**: from now on the read endpoints, the `Alert`, `BaseSentinel` and `Storage` change only with a new major version (an addition that old clients can ignore is allowed and noted here). The message of the product is the same in the README, the guides and the help: Lite is the simple edition for one person on one computer, Complete is the control centre (several accounts, a team, a service and clients). Nothing else in the behaviour of the monitor changes in this version.

### Added

- **The live events as a stream (Complete, off by default)**: with `live.sse.enabled` on, `GET /api/live-events/stream` sends the events of the incoming webhook as they are accepted, as server-sent events: a `hello` frame (how many are held), one `live` frame per event with a running `id` (resume with `Last-Event-ID` or `?since=`; only the closed list of fields of `GET /api/live-events` is ever sent), a keep-alive comment and a final `bye`. It is read only, asks for the access token in the network mode like any other request, keeps at most `live.sse.max_clients` listeners (more get `429`) each for `live.sse.max_seconds`, and the Lite edition does not have it. The three settings are in the Settings tab (sub-tab Incoming webhook) with their help in the eight languages, the guide of the incoming webhook explains it, and the references of the two skills list the endpoint. A test with a real server covers off by default, the limit of listeners and an accepted event reaching the listener.

### Added

- **Presets of AI providers and a table of compatible AIs**: a versioned file of data (`ai_presets.json`, served read only at `GET /api/ai/presets`) lists twelve hosted services (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, xAI Grok, Mistral, DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Perplexity, Cohere) and six local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM, LocalAI, Jan) with editable example models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, Phi, gpt-oss; no weights, no downloads). In the AI settings a selector fills the provider, the address, the NAME of the environment variable of the key and a model, shows the privacy of the choice (text sent over the internet or kept on this computer) and says "compatible by protocol, not tested with this tool" where it is so; none is active by default and the key never leaves its environment variable. A server on this computer (`http://127.0.0.1:...`) may now be saved as `ai.base_url` and may work without a key; a remote address still needs https and its key. The three AI guides carry the table in the eight languages, and a fake server with the OpenAI protocol tests the answers 200, 401, 429 and a timeout, with the key absent from every output.

### Added

- **Apprise as a channel of notifications (Complete, off by default)**: `notify.channels.apprise` hands the message to the `apprise` command, if it is installed, so that any service Apprise knows can be reached. The addresses (they hold the secrets of those services) are read from the environment variable named by `urls_env`, written to a private temporary file for the instant of the call and removed, never put in the arguments, and the command gets an environment without the keys of the monitor. Apprise opens its own connections, so the guard of the monitor on private addresses does not apply to it: the channel has its own switch, marked as a security setting. A missing command is the reason `not_installed`, a failure is counted and never stops the monitor.
- **A log of actions (Complete only, on by default)**: next to the audit of the accesses, `logs/audit_actions.jsonl` keeps one JSON line for each change (who, what, when, on which account): a change of settings (the names of the settings, never their values), a silence and its removal, a change of users, passwords, notification preferences or credentials. Each line carries the hash of the one before it, so a line that is changed, cut out or put in later is found (`GET /api/audit-log` says where the chain breaks); past `audit_log.max_mb` the old part is kept as one more file and the chain goes on. No value and no secret is ever written (a key that looks like a secret is dropped, every text is cleaned and cut). An administrator reads it, and a maintainer only when `audit_log.maintainers_can_read` is on. Three settings in the Sentinel tab and the guide AUDIT_LOG.md in the eight languages.

- **Scheduled reports (Complete only, off by default)**: the monitor writes a report of the account on a cron schedule (`report_schedule.cron`, five fields in the local time, `0 8 * * 1` by default) or when an administrator asks at this computer: the score (no number while it is calibrating or has too little data), what changed since the last report, the repositories that need a person and the open alerts, as one HTML page with a print style (a PDF is the print-to-PDF of the browser) and as Markdown. It is made from what the monitor already holds, asks GitHub for nothing and sends nothing: the files stay in `data/reports/`, the oldest runs go after `report_schedule.keep`, a report is written once for each scheduled minute (a long stop gives one, not a pile), the first one waits for the first scheduled minute after the switch-on, a failure is noted and tried again at the next one, and every text from the data is escaped. The Team tab lists the files and has the button "Write a report now"; `GET /api/report-files`, `GET /api/report-files/file?name=` (only a file the service wrote for the account) and `POST /api/report-files/run` are the routes. Five settings in the Sentinel tab, the guide REPORT_SCHEDULE.md in the eight languages.
- **A harness and the reproductions of the independent review, in the repository**: `tools/audit_harness.py --check` starts, with no GitHub, a supervisor with three accounts (alpha, beta, default) and four users (administrator, maintainer of alpha only, viewer of beta only, one switched off), asks the routes that decide the isolation of the accounts and prints what each user gets; `tests/test_193_regressions.py` holds the reproductions of the review of 1.8.3 (accounts of a request, accounts kept when a password changes, silences of a remote maintainer, the test message and its hourly limit, a restored copy and revoked sessions, the lock and the administrator, the keys a started program does not inherit).

### Changed

- **A test no longer reads a file of the person who wrote it**: the check against the real file of the profile repository runs only when `MONITOR_REAL_CENTRAL_FILE` says where it is.

### Added

- **The health of each repository and of the team (Complete only)**: from what the monitor already holds (runs, red and stuck workflows, the open alerts of the three sentinels and the readiness of the releases) a state is worked out for each repository (bad, warning, OK or not seen) with a risk number; a repository that no sentinel looked at, or that one could not read, never comes out as OK and says who did not see it fully. `GET /api/repos/<owner>/<repo>/health` gives the detail and `GET /api/team/health` the ranking, the totals, the numbers by ecosystem and by sentinel and the filters (ecosystem, least severity, a piece of the name). They never call GitHub.
- **The Team tab and the detail of a repository**: the ranking with the repositories that need a person first, three filters, and a window with the CI, the alerts, the release and the activity when a repository is clicked; the deep links `?view=team`, `?view=repos` and `?view=repo&repo=owner/name` (with `chrome=0` for wall screens) open each view. The Lite edition does not have it.
- **The `team` command**: `monitor_cli.py team` prints the ranking (`--severity warn|bad`) and `team --repo owner/name` the detail of one, with `--json`; read only and from the same routes as the page. The guide HEALTH.md, in the eight languages, explains it all.

### Added

- **Security is a part of the score**: the points that the open findings of the Security sentinel take off 100 (a critical alert, a high one, a secret, a branch with no protection, workflows with write permission) are the fifth part, with the weight `score.weights.security` (25 by default) and its own limits; it only counts while the sentinel is on and has looked at enough repositories, and without it the answer says that the number is not complete and the other parts are rescaled. The security figures are the same in the window and in the one before it, because GitHub gives no history of them.

### Changed

- **The default weights of the score are now 30, 15, 15, 15 and 25** (reliability, speed, recovery, collaboration, security) so that the fifth part has room; they are settings, as before.
- **A window with runs and no failure has nothing to recover**: the recovery part is full in that case, as a fact and no longer as a missing piece of data, so a healthy account is not told that it has too little data once there are five parts.
- **The Security sentinel (Complete only, off by default)**: the third sentinel reads, without writing anything to GitHub, the open Dependabot, code scanning and secret scanning alerts, whether the default branch has protection, whether the workflows get write permission by default and, if asked, whether there is a CODEOWNERS file, and raises one alert per repository and signal in the Alerts tab (origin Security), with the counts by severity. A source GitHub does not answer for a repository (the feature is off, or the login may not read it) is listed as unreadable and is never taken for a clean bill of health. It has its own cycle, a cap of repositories per round, conditional reads and a pause while the allowance is low, writes the events security_new and security_fixed for the notification channels (nothing at the first look), has a box in the Sentinel tab, in the preferences of each user and in the settings (`sentinels.security.enabled` and twelve more, with the weights of its penalty in the file), a route at /api/sentinel/security, a guide (SENTINEL_SECURITY.md) in the eight languages and a filter by origin. The cost and the signals are tunable one by one.
- **Every sentinel tells its lifecycle**: healthy, degraded (some reads fail, a source cannot be read or the first look is not finished), paused (waiting for the allowance), error (it fails and has read nothing) or off, so that no alerts is never mistaken for could not look. The Collab and Security sentinels carry it in their status.

Each pass writes the snapshot of the hour with the answer of the score and a breakdown by repository (the worst first). The ledger keeps only what two windows need and at most 20000 runs, and a failure of the pass is counted and never stops the refresh. Nothing is shown yet: the page, the API and the command follow.

- **The score of an account is kept: one snapshot per account and hour, in both storages**: the database gets a new table (schema 2; the migration runs in one transaction and an interrupted one leaves the database as it was), the files get one file per account. The snapshots travel with the export, the backup and the migration between storages, are compared by the check of a migration, and are removed by the retention pass with the days of the analytics. A monitor that still runs the previous schema refuses to open a database already moved to schema 2, as it always did with a newer one.
- **The score of an account turns its metrics into a number from 0 to 100, a letter from A to E and a trend**: a weighted sum of four parts (reliability of the CI 40, speed 20, recovery 20, collaboration 20; the weights and the limits of every part are settings), compared with the window before. It never shows a number it cannot stand behind: an account watched for less than a day is "calibrating", one with fewer than 20 finished runs or with too little of the weight backed by data is "not enough data", and every answer carries its coverage, the quality of the data and the parts not collected yet, so 85 is never read as "all clear".
- **The metrics behind the account score are collected from the data the monitor already has**: success rate, the median and the 95th percentile of the duration, the time a failing workflow takes to recover, runs per day, how long collaboration items stay open and how many are still open, for any window of time. A number with nothing behind it is reported as missing and never as zero, and the amount of data behind every number is kept, so the score can say that there is not enough data instead of inventing one.

### Fixed

- **Team mode with several accounts: the account of a request is decided once**: the gate of the team mode and the forwarding to the monitor of the account read `account` in two different ways, so a request that repeated it was judged for the account of the user and served from another one. Now one function decides the account, the gate judges that value and the same value is forwarded, a request that gives `account` more than once answers 400 `account_repeated`, and the process of each account refuses a user the supervisor resolved for another account.

- **A new password or role no longer moves a person to another account**: changing only the password or only the role of a user (in the page, in the API or with the console reset) kept nothing of their assigned accounts and left them with the main one; the accounts they had are kept unless the request names others or the user becomes an administrator.

- **The person at the computer can create the first administrator through the local port, and is never locked out of their own login**: with a reverse proxy declared the first administrator could not be created from the second local port; and wrong passwords from the network no longer lock out the person who is at the computer of the monitor. A name that does not exist is now counted and locked like a real one, so "locked" does not tell which names exist.

- **The test message of a user counts against the hourly limit** of messages of that user, like any other notice.

- **The e-mail channel works with its default sender**: the default sender at `localhost` was refused as a bad value without saying which field; it is accepted, and a wrong sender is reported as `bad_sender`.

- **`gh-token --read-only` hands out a token that can only read**: it is asked for apart from the one the monitor keeps, with read permissions only, and the command refuses to print it when the answer carries a write permission.

- **The supervisor key and the access token leave the environment of the process**: both are read once at start and taken out of the environment, so `gh`, `git` and the command of a notice do not inherit them.

- **Behind the Docker Compose proxy, one visitor's wrong tokens no longer lock out everybody**: Caddy is another container, so every visitor reached the monitor with the address of the proxy. The new `listen.trusted_proxies` setting (`MONITOR_TRUSTED_PROXIES`) names the address or network of the proxy, and the Compose file gives its network a fixed range (`MONITOR_SUBNET`).

- **The guide says what the code does for silencing and acknowledging**: a maintainer silences and acknowledges alerts from the computer of the monitor only, never from the network, in the eight languages of the guide.
- **The migration of the product folder can be undone even when it was cut half way**: what is about to move is written to the journal before it moves, with paths relative to the folder, so a power cut or a kill in the middle no longer leaves moved files that nothing remembers, and a folder renamed or mounted elsewhere after the migration still undoes. The undo deletes the journal only when everything it lists is back; otherwise it keeps what could not be put back.
- **A symbolic link is never moved by the migration**: a configuration file that is a relative link would have been left broken in its new folder. It stays where it is and the start says so.
- **A backup no longer carries the sessions and restoring one never brings a revoked session back**: the backup left out the sessions (they hold the token against forged requests of each one), and a restore ignores them even in a backup made by an older version.
- **The log of a failed step refuses an id that is not plain digits** (a superscript digit passed the check and raised an error) with the same answer as any other bad request.
- **`--help` and the other flags that only answer work while a monitor is running**: the check that stops a second monitor on the same port ran before the flags were read, so `--help` (and the quality gate of a release that calls it) failed on a computer where the monitor was already on port 8765. And the tests that measure real seconds take their limit from the load of the computer, so a busy runner no longer fails them.

- The notification kinds `credential_blind` and `credential_back` are new; `credential_blind` is in the default list and in the example configuration. The Alerts tab, `/api/alerts` and the command line know the level `critical` and the sentinel `system`, and a critical alert is listed first.

- `--doctor` tells the login of each account apart by its own credential file too, so two accounts that each got a replacement are not reported as sharing one token.

- The time limits of the release gate are 3600 seconds by default (they were 900 and 1800, too short for a loaded computer). `MONITOR_RELEASE_TEST_TIMEOUT` and `MONITOR_RELEASE_CLEAN_TIMEOUT` change them (60 to 86400 seconds), and the default is read when the gate runs, not when the module is loaded.

### Added

- **The allowance of GitHub can be shared by kind of read, with a reserve for your tools, and it is counted as a sum**: `readpool.prefer.<kind>` names the source (user, GitHub App, second account) that answers a kind of read first (runs, security alerts, issues and pull requests, history, discovery, the rest; `auto` keeps the spread of always) and `readpool.reserve.<source>` keeps that many calls free in a source, so the `gh` of your tools and agents always finds some in the allowance of the user. A source that fails or is under its reserve hands the read to the others; writes and actions keep the token of the user. The bar of the allowance and the working modes count the SUM of all the sources; its tooltip shows each one and the Quota tab adds the total. Both settings are in the Quota tab in eight languages.

- **A map of the monitor for the AIs that talk to it**: `ai/INDEX.json` lists every file of the `ai/` folder (purpose, format, who writes it, when it changes), the real path of every folder of the monitor and the endpoints of the running monitor, so an AI, local or external, never depends on a fixed path; `ai/README.md` explains the folder to an AI that has never seen it. Both are rewritten at every start. `GET /api/paths` answers with the folders in use, the main files and what is still in the old places, in both editions and in the supervisor of several accounts.

- **The tests of the new order**: the table of places, the folders that move, the migration of an installation of 1.7.x and of 1.8.0 (clean root, same bytes, the copy of the configuration, a second run that does nothing, a file that is never overwritten, the undo), the index and the map for the AIs, the places the gate script finds, and the entry points in `bin/`.

- **Official Docker image and service mode**: `deploy/Dockerfile` is multi-stage (the GitHub CLI from its signed apt repository, the compiled code without the tests, and a final image with only Python, `gh`, the CA certificates and the code, read-only and owned by root). It runs as the user 10001, never as root, with two volumes (`/config` and `/data`), `tini` as init and a health check that is the deep one. `python -m github_actions_monitor.service` prepares everything a person does by hand before the first start from documented environment variables: the configuration, the first account (or several with `MONITOR_ACCOUNTS`), the keys of `listen` and `auth`, and an access token that is made once, kept with mode 600 and never printed. `MONITOR_CONFIG` places the configuration file outside the code.

- **Compose with a reverse proxy, and systemd**: `deploy/compose.yaml` (code read-only, no capabilities, the login as a Docker secret) with an optional Caddy in front (`deploy/Caddyfile`; TLS by itself for a public name, its own authority for a private one, or none), `deploy/.env.example`, and, for a classic install, `deploy/github-actions-monitor.service` with its env file (hardened, restarts on failure, checks the deep health after the start, reloads the credential files on `systemctl reload`). The guide `DEPLOYMENT.md` in the eight languages lists every environment variable, the first start as a service, the backup, the upgrade and the check of the attestation of the image.

- **Image for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` in ghcr.io**: the workflow `release-image.yml` builds and publishes it when a release is published (or by hand), with the minimum permissions of each job, every action pinned by commit, a time limit on every job, tags `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y` and `latest`, and an attestation of the provenance. Pushing is a separate step that only a release takes: the same workflow builds without pushing when started by hand with `push` off, and the CI builds the image on every change.

- **A deep health check**: `/api/health?deep=1` (see above), `python -m github_actions_monitor.cli.healthcheck` for a container or a service manager (exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3) and `monitor_cli.py health --deep` from any computer. An account whose GitHub login is no good is named but is not a failure: a restart does not fix a lost login.

- **A login that GitHub revokes or lets expire marks only that account as blind**: after two refusals in a row that say the login itself is no good (401, `Bad credentials`, expired or revoked token, suspended account, no login) the account is blind; the others go on. The page, `/api/accounts` (`state: blind`), the health check and the command line say so, a critical system alert (`system.credential_blind`) opens once, the channels are told once (`credential_blind`, and `credential_back` when it works again) and the account keeps trying. A refusal of one permission (a 403 for one repository) does not make an account blind. A service that starts with a login that is already no good stays up and blind instead of giving up.

- **The login can be replaced without restarting anything**: the endpoint `/api/accounts/<id>/credential` (an `admin` session in the team mode; the computer of the monitor otherwise), `monitor_cli.py credential replace --account ID --new-token-file FILE` (or `-` for the standard input; a token is never taken from a flag), and SIGHUP where the system has it (every account reads its credential files again). The new token is checked against GitHub BEFORE it is kept, so a token GitHub refuses changes nothing; a good one is kept only in the folder of that account (mode 600) and used at once. `GH_TOKEN_FILE` names a file for the login of all the accounts, read at the start and on SIGHUP. The token is never in an answer, a log, an alert or the audit.

- **The supervisor of several accounts listens in the network mode** like the monitor of one account: the access token on every request (cookie, header or `/api/access`), lock-out after wrong tokens, the `Host` check, optional TLS with your certificate, the second port of the person at the computer (`listen.local_port`), and the keys that decide exposure, the login of GitHub and the actions on GitHub only from the computer of the monitor (the account treats a request from the network as remote).

- **The page and the tools say where the monitor listens**: this computer, the network or behind a proxy (`listen.proxy_public_host`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.trusted_proxy`), in the bottom bar of the page, in `/api/accounts`, `/api/health` and the first lines of `monitor_cli.py status` and `monitor_cli.py accounts`.

- **The command line works against a monitor on another computer**: `--url` or `MONITOR_URL`, `--ca-file` or `MONITOR_CA_FILE` to trust the authority of an HTTPS certificate of your own, and in the team mode `--user` with `--password-file` (or `MONITOR_USER`, `MONITOR_PASSWORD_FILE`) to sign in with a Bearer session (`auth.allow_bearer`). `status` and `accounts` end with exit code 3 for an account that is blind.

- **Tests**: a test of the container in the CI that builds the image, starts it read-only and without root, revokes the login of one of two accounts and checks that only that account turns blind, that the critical alert opens, that the deep health check stays green, that a refused token changes nothing, that a good one brings the account back without a restart, and that SIGHUP does the same; and one regression test for each behaviour of a revoked login (the count, the other accounts, the alert, the notice, the replacement, the file, SIGHUP, the roles, the audit and the token that never appears).

### Fixed

- **A second monitor on the same port no longer starts, and openssl is found outside the PATH**: on Windows the port of the monitor is bound for the monitor alone, so two processes can no longer listen on 8765 at once, and a start that finds a monitor already answering on its port says so and stops instead of taking another one. `openssl` is searched in the PATH, in the places where Git for Windows keeps it and in the usual folders of macOS and Linux (a monitor started from a `.bat` or a service finds it); `github_app.openssl_path` chooses one by hand, the status of the App shows `openssl_path` and the doctor says which one signs when it is not the one of the PATH.

- **A failure that the monitor swallows on purpose leaves a line in its log**: every `degraded` count now also writes one line to the log file with the origin, the kind of error, the place in the code where it was raised, the cleaned message (never a token) and the count; a failure that repeats writes its first twenty lines and then one in twenty-five, and the recent failures of the doctor and the page carry the place too. Before, the reason was only on the console.

- **The network mode does not start before the first administrator exists**: with `auth.enabled` and `listen.network` both on and no user yet, the monitor stops at the start and says how to go on (turn `listen.network` off, start the monitor, create the administrator from this computer, turn it on and start again). The local mode and the individual mode start as always.

- **The OpenTelemetry export obeys the rule for outgoing requests**: a collector on this computer is called directly and a redirect from it is not followed; any other collector is refused when it, or a redirect, leads to a loopback, private, link-local or metadata address (unless the setting that allows private targets is on), and the proxy of the environment is not used. Before, the export used a plain request that followed every redirect.

- **The proxy of the environment is said to be a frontier of trust**: the help of its setting (and the code) now say that the proxy resolves the name again on its own, so the check before the proxy is a first filter, not a guarantee, and that it should be turned on only behind a managed proxy that refuses loopback, private, link-local and metadata destinations. It stays off by default.

- **A test keeps the page from putting free text into markup without escaping it**: every text of the API that goes into a markup string passes through the escaping function, and the two places that write it as plain text are listed; the help documents are checked to escape their markup and to refuse scripts and non-web links.

- **A name with a line feed at the end is no longer a valid name**: the checks of account ids, repository names, keys, owners, addresses and the like ended in the end-of-line mark, which also accepts a text that is followed by one more line feed ("alpha" and "alpha" plus a line feed were the same id). They now end at the end of the text, 76 checks in all, and a test keeps every new check that way.

- **The pause of the hook of an AI tool is kept in one step**: reading the last moment and writing the new one take a lock, so two events at the same time cannot both pass; and when the moment cannot be written the answer is "do not block", not "ok" (before, a failed write still allowed the block and the pause was never applied).

- **The exporter of a self-hosted runner can no longer send the monitor somewhere else**: a redirect is followed only to this computer or a private address, with the same scheme, no credentials, and at most three times; a public host, another scheme or a loop ends the read with no figures. No proxy is used for it.

- **Calls to GitHub that never return are counted, and the monitor stops piling them up**: when a call gives up waiting its thread is remembered until it ends; with `watchdog_max_abandoned` of them (8 by default, 0 = no limit) still alive the monitor starts no new call to GitHub, and the deep health check answers "degraded" with the number, instead of restarting the loop again and again while threads and connections pile up.

- **Each account has its own feed for the AIs**: with several accounts, every account process keeps its alerts, its brief and the ledger of the notices to an external AI in its own folder (ai/accounts/ and the id of the account) instead of one folder that all of them rewrote. An alert carries its account and its id depends on it, so the same workflow red in two accounts is two alerts; the refresh of one account closes only its own alerts (before, an account closed the alerts of the others because they were not in its snapshot). Installations with one account change nothing. The alerts that an older version left in the shared folder stay there and are closed by the account of the product folder.

- **Refresh, acknowledgement and status of the feed for the AIs are one step at a time**: they take the same lock, between threads and between processes that share a folder, so an acknowledgement is no longer undone by a refresh that read the state a moment before. A refresh that cannot get the lock in ten seconds is skipped and tried again at the next cycle; the diagnosis of a log is read before the lock is taken.

- **The cap of notices to an external AI cannot be passed by notices that run at the same time**: the calls and the cost of the hour are checked and reserved in one locked step before anything is sent, also across processes that share the ledger. A reservation made by a process that died before sending counts until its hour is over.

- **With the team mode on and no user yet, only the person at this computer gets in**: until the first administrator exists a request from anywhere else (the network, or through a proxy) is answered 403 "create the first administrator from this computer first" for everything that is not public (health check, login page, webhook); before, the whole monitor stayed open to the network during that time. Turning the team mode on changes nothing for the person at this computer, who still creates the first administrator from the login page.

- **The process of each account answers only to its supervisor**: it asks for the key the supervisor gave it when it started it, on every request; another user of the same machine who reaches the port of an account process gets a 403 instead of the data, whatever the team mode says.

- The test of an account that dies at once no longer depends on the speed of the computer: the wait before an account is started again is checked with a clock that the test gives, and a second test checks the schedule of the waits without reading the real time (the old one failed under load in the gate of a release).

- **Saving the settings never goes on without the lock of the file**: when another process keeps the lock for more than ten seconds the save is refused with "another process is saving the settings: try again in a moment" and nothing is written; before, it went on after the wait and could undo the save of the other process.

- **The command of the sentinel is checked before it is run**: it has to be a list whose first word is the full path of a program that is not a shell (not sh, bash, cmd, powershell and the like), with no shell characters in any word, no word with a blank after the first, and no flag that makes a program read a command line (-c, /c, -Command). Anything else is not run at all.

- **Tokens for scripts are off by default**: the login with the client "api" and the Authorization: Bearer header are refused until the setting for tokens for scripts and apps is turned on in the Advanced tab; the browser session is unchanged. A token or a password never reaches the audit file.

### Fixed

- **The "loading repositories" box stays on the page after the last repository is read**: the finished picture now reaches the page as soon as the reading ends, without waiting for the upkeep that follows it (the brief for the AI tools, the alert centre), and a long list of Sentinel panels can no longer make that brief loop for ever (it was the loop that kept the last partial picture, 131 / 131, on the page).

- **Reloading the page (F5) no longer takes minutes to get the data**: the endless loop of the brief used all the processor time of the monitor and the page gave up with an abort; besides, the answer of the data endpoint was written to the connection with the global lock held, so one stalled connection (a closed tab) froze every other page and the refresh cycle. The lock is now held only to take the picture. A browser test checks that the box shows while loading and leaves with the last repository, and server tests check that the brief ends, that the finished picture is published before the upkeep and that a stalled connection does not block a reload.

### Changed

- **New folder layout, same behaviour**: the code is now an importable package in `src/github_actions_monitor/` (`app`, `accounts`, `sentinels`, `security`, `data_pipeline`, `integrations`, `cli`, `ui`, `i18n`, `util`); the page, the neutral examples with `quotas.json` and the eight language catalogues are in `assets/` (`static`, `examples`, `locales`); `make_release.py` is in `tools/`. The launchers stay in the product folder and start `python -m github_actions_monitor` (complete) or `python -m github_actions_monitor.lite` (lite): same address, same port. The data of the person who runs it (`actions_monitor.json`, caches, logs, `accounts/`, catalogues) still lives next to the launchers, never inside `src/`.

- The commands of the guides (`python read_report.py`, `python actions_monitor.py --doctor`, `python monitor_cli.py status` ...) keep working: a small entry-point file with the same name stays in the product folder, so the hooks and MCP servers already registered by path keep working too. The release zip keeps its folder name and now carries `src/`, `assets/` and `tools/`.

- **The roadmap tells what 1.8.0 holds and what each next version brings**: what is already in the main branch, what is finished and waiting to be merged, what is still being finished, and the plan from 1.8.2 to 2.0.0 in the order it will be done, in the eight languages.

- **The bar at the foot of the page is one line and says only what the boxes at the top do not**: the connection, the allowance, the runs, the last read and the repositories were said twice (as boxes at the top and as items of the bar); the bar keeps the sentinels, the Low-mode warning (the only mode it says), the AI, the account, the version, the address, the sound chip and the clock, and it no longer wraps at any width (on a narrow screen the date and the zone leave first). A browser test measures it in several languages, wide and narrow.
- **The "loading repositories" box** is checked in a browser: it is shown while repositories load and it is gone with the last one.

### Added

- **Storage layer** (`src/github_actions_monitor/storage/`): a `Storage` interface (configuration, sentinel state, the event feed, analytics, small named documents and the global records of users, their accounts and sessions) that keeps the rule "a write is atomic, a damaged item reads as empty" for every backend. `FileStorage` is the first backend and keeps the layout of `accounts/<id>/` exactly as before (and the flat installation next to the launchers): the same files with the same names, written through a temporary file that is flushed and renamed. `create_storage` is the one place that picks the backend; the lite edition always gets the file backend.

- Backups of a storage that any backend can restore: one `.zip` with a dump and a manifest of counts, size and SHA-256; the restore verifies the copy first and refuses to write over a storage that already holds accounts unless it is forced.

- **SQLite backend** (optional, off by default): the same data in a database, one file per account (`accounts/<id>/storage.sqlite3`), so the process of an account is the only one that writes it. WAL journal and a busy timeout, every write one short transaction, versioned schema migrations that run in the same transaction as the bump of the version (an interrupted one leaves the database as it was; a database from a newer version is refused), an index on the events of an account by time, and a process killed in the middle of a write recovers on the next start. The state that moves to the database: the event feed, what the feed announced, the analytics, the state of the sentinels, the silences and the update notice; the configuration stays a JSON file (it is what names the backend), and caches and logs stay files. The lite edition has no such option and always uses files.

- A shared database for the whole installation (several accounts and processes in one file) is kept ready and tested: WAL, busy timeout, two processes ticking at once and a reader that never waits for a writer.

- `tools/migrate_storage.py` moves the state between the file backend and SQLite in either direction: a dry run by default, `--apply` copies every account in one step and then reads both sides back and compares every item and every event; your files are never changed or deleted; an interrupted run leaves each account whole or as it was and the same command resumes. `tools/backup_storage.py` makes, checks and restores the backups of either backend (a backup of files restores into SQLite and the other way round).

- **Retention and rotation** (Complete): a monitor that runs for months no longer grows without a ceiling. `retention.events_days` (90 by default) and `retention.analytics_days` (180) set how long the events and the days of the analytics history are kept; `retention.mode` is `archive` (default; the old events are first written to a `.gz` in `events/archive/` of the account, outside the hot path, then removed from the feed) or `delete`; `retention.enabled` is the switch and `retention.interval_hours` (24) says how often a short pass runs at the end of a refresh. Each pass leaves a line in an audit document (when, how many events removed and kept, the archive file, how many analytics days, any error). The purge only removes events and analytics days older than their limit: never the configuration, the state of the sentinels, the silences, nor an event that has no time. `retention.events_max_kb` (512, as before) is the separate ceiling in size of the feed file with the file backend. The settings are in the Folders and files tab; the lite edition does not have them.

- `--doctor` has two new checks: the storage (SQLite database present, passes its integrity check and has a schema this version understands, read only, nothing is created or migrated) and the retention (the size of the events of each account against `retention.warn_events_mb`, and a warning for a monitor that runs as a service, on the network, without a browser or in a container, whose configuration has no retention block).

- `tools/migrate_layout.py` for a folder that was a flat installation: a dry run by default; `--apply` copies your configuration to `layout_backup_<stamp>/config/` and MOVES (never deletes, never overwrites) the old modules, page, examples and `locales/` to `layout_backup_<stamp>/old_code/`. `--doctor` warns while such leftovers exist. `MIGRATING.md` describes it in the eight languages.

- **Team mode: users, roles and sessions** (`src/github_actions_monitor/security/auth.py`, `auth_http.py`, `auth_cli.py`; off by default with `auth.enabled`, so one person alone notices nothing): once the first administrator exists (created at `/login` or on the console, only from the computer that runs the monitor and only once) every request needs a session. Roles `viewer` (reads), `maintainer` (also silences, acknowledges, changes the working mode) and `admin` (also settings, users and everything that can reach GitHub); a route nobody listed is closed to all but an admin. Each user has the accounts they may see: another account asked for with `?account=`, `X-Account-Id` or an export answers 403. Passwords are kept as a salted scrypt hash; the session is an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (Secure over HTTPS) with a CSRF token on every POST, or a Bearer token for scripts and apps (`auth.allow_bearer`); a user is locked after `auth.max_failed_logins` wrong passwords, each address is rate-limited, a changed password, role or state ends the user's sessions and there is always one active administrator. Endpoints `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/users` and `/api/auth/audit` answer errors as `{"error", "code"}`; `auth_audit.jsonl` records logins, locks, refused requests and user changes without any secret. The lite edition never has a login, the one-use token of the page still applies, and `python -m github_actions_monitor.security.auth_cli` recovers a lost administrator password. Seven settings (`auth.*`) with their help in the eight languages and a section in `docs/ADVANCED.md` in the eight languages; `tests/test_auth.py` covers the rules, the roles of every kind of route, the scope between accounts, the cookie, CSRF, Bearer, locks and the audit on the real server.

- The accounts supervisor filters by user: `GET /api/accounts`, `/api/accounts/<id>/status`, the page of an account and every request with `?account=` or `X-Account-Id` show and reach only the accounts assigned to the user (an admin sees all), and the monitor of an account is told who is acting. A silence of the Alerts tab now keeps who made it: `muted_by` in `GET /api/alerts` and in the history of silences.

- **The page says when it is out of step with the monitor**: the bottom bar shows "data from Ns ago" (the time since the last good answer) and turns red, with the connection lamp, after 60 seconds; a failed request shows "retrying in N s" and retries by itself; a request that hangs is cut after 15 seconds; a watchdog asks again when the page is late and nothing is on the way, and coming back to the tab asks at once. Data that stop changing for two minutes (longer in low mode) count as old. When the page comes back from a gap it asks again for the sentinels, the history and the mode.

- **The sound can be unlocked and no longer misses a red that came while the page was closed**: a visible notice "Sound blocked by the browser: click here to turn it on" appears while the browser keeps the audio locked (any click on the page unlocks it; the notice button also plays a test tone); the page remembers the reds it had seen (per account, up to six hours), so a red that appeared while the page was closed or reloading sounds; and when the page returns from a gap the cooldown no longer hides a new red. The help of `sound.server_beep` (off by default, this computer only) now says what the page cannot do and what that switch adds, in the eight languages.

- **The refresh loop has a heartbeat and a watchdog**: `/api/data` now carries `loop` (the phase of the cycle, how long it has been running, the last good cycle, the last error and the phase it happened in, the restarts and any problem writing the log or the brief for the AI). The page says "The monitor does not refresh: its cycle has been in <phase> for <time>" in the bottom bar when a cycle runs far too long, and a log or brief that cannot be written is shown there too instead of failing in silence. A watchdog thread checks every 30 seconds: a cycle that runs longer than the new setting `watchdog_minutes` (default 10, 0 = off) or a loop whose thread is gone is restarted in a new thread, after writing the traceback of every thread to the log file (where it hangs). The old loop, if it ever wakes up, sees it was replaced and leaves without publishing.

- **The "bing bing" also sounds when the page loses the monitor itself**: once per loss (no answer for over a minute, or a cycle stuck), together with the red bar. The mute chip, the `sound.on_connection_lost` switch, the cooldown and the browser's sound lock apply as for any other sound; the help of that setting says so in the eight languages.

- **GraphQL for quiet repositories** (`network.graphql_checks`, off by default; `network.graphql_batch`, 1 to 30, 20 by default; in the Quota tab, in the eight languages): the repositories that are not hot are read in batches through GraphQL, which has an allowance of its own, instead of one REST call each; the hot ones and any repository the query does not answer are still read through REST in the same cycle, and a failed batch falls back to REST. It sees only the last commit of the default branch and gives no durations, attempts or other branches (the guide of the allowance says so). The accounting (batches, repositories, points, repositories sent to REST) is part of the allowance line of the brief and of the state for the AI tools, next to the reads answered `304`.

- **The active notice to an external AI** (`ai_notify.*`, in the AI tab, local-only, off by default, in the eight languages): when a NEW real alert opens, a short summary goes to the provider of the AI block and its answer is kept as advice in `ai_notify.jsonl`. A first confirmation per provider (`ai_notify.confirmed_provider`, changing the provider needs a new one), only the redacted fields of a closed list (severity, class, repository, workflow, conclusion, streak, cause, next step, link), a cap of calls an hour and a cap of declared cost an hour (a call is counted before it is made), the key by the name of an environment variable, and the AI never runs an action (its answer is cut, its links are defused and nothing of it is read as a command). The variant of an outgoing command (`ai_notify.command` (only in the configuration file, never in the Settings page)) names ONE file by its absolute path, started without a shell and without arguments, that receives the same JSON on its standard input. The notice leaves from a thread of its own, so a slow provider never holds a cycle.

- **The terminal application edits lists and maps**: in the Settings tab of `tui_textual.py`, a list (the items separated by commas) and a map of numbers (`name=3, other=5`) can be typed and saved like a simple setting; the server checks every value again, the options of security still change only in the page, and the guide of the console tools says so.

- **The page of the team mode shows who is signed in**: a box in the header with the name and the role (a text, not only a colour) that opens a menu to change the password, to see and manage the users and the audit (administrators only) and to sign out; the first time, with the mode on and no user yet, it points to `/login`. Every change the page sends carries the CSRF token, a session that ended sends the person to `/login`, and a wrong token is renewed and tried once. In the individual mode and in the lite edition the page draws nothing and asks nothing new; `tests/test_auth_page.py` runs the wrapper of `fetch` in Node against a fake network.

- **Every status lamp has a shape as well as a colour**: a tick for ok, an exclamation mark for warn, a cross for bad, an i for info and a question mark for unknown, in the lamps of the sentinels and in the lamp of the bar at the foot, so the level never depends on the colour alone.

- **The lamps are alive**: each one breathes at a pace that follows its level (slow when all is well, quick when something is red) with a soft glow of its own colour.

- **A lamp that changes plays one short transition**, and the tooltip of the lamps of the sentinels says what the level was before (also for a keyboard user, with the focus on the lamp).

- **The boxes at the top answer when their state changes**: a short pop when a box turns red, yellow, green or starts running, a small tick when a figure changes and a slight bob of the icon of the active runs.

- **Hover and focus say more**: the lamps of the sentinels lift and show their text in a tip that follows the keyboard focus too, and the rows of the alerts answer to the pointer.

- **Filters move**: when you change a filter, the rows that are drawn arrive with a short slide instead of jumping.

- **Less motion means no motion**: with the preference of the system for reduced motion nothing breathes, pops or slides, and the light edition keeps its figures and its bar with the same lamps. No library was added.

- A check of the life of the page in a real browser (the lamps are animated, every lamp has a shape and a text, a changed lamp plays its transition, the same page with reduced motion stands still, nothing is logged as an error), run by the job of the page.

### Fixed

- The dashboard could stay on one old picture while the monitor was running: a call to `gh` that never returned (a child process holding its pipes after the timeout) held the refresh loop for good while the page still answered at once. Every `gh` call is now bounded by a hard deadline in a helper thread, and a loop that still hangs is found and restarted by the watchdog above.
- A failure to write the log was swallowed and could end a cycle; it is now kept and shown, and the cycle goes on.
- The page showed old data without any warning when the monitor stopped or answered slowly (a request that never returned left the page looking alive), and the "bing bing" stayed silent after a reload or a long gap.
- The SQLite storage no longer fails with "database is locked" when several processes open or write the same database at once: the wait for another writer is 30 seconds by default and can be set with `busy_timeout_ms` in the `storage` block, and the steps that SQLite does not make wait (the first switch to WAL, taking the writer lock) are tried again a few times with growing pauses.
- The brief for the AI tools (`ALERTS_BRIEF.md`) and the log (`actions_monitor_log.txt`) now agree with a monitor that is running: the brief has a `Monitor:` line (cycle complete, cycle in progress, connection lost, last cycle failed) and the hour of that note, so a cycle that is still reading repositories no longer leaves the hour of the previous cycle as the last word (the alerts it lists are the ones kept from the last complete cycle, and a partial cycle never opens or closes one); the log writes a `cycle=started` line when a cycle begins.

- **The stream of events for AIs no longer dies on an ordinary log line**: the line of the feed is cleaned field by field and then written, instead of cleaning a JSON that was already written (a cause that ended in `password: x`, `token=x` or `DB_PASSWORD=x` broke it). A line that cannot be cleaned is skipped and the stream goes on; the answers of the MCP server are cleaned the same way. In the cleaner, the value of a `key=value` pair stops at a quote, a comma or a semicolon, and a quoted value is cleaned whole.
